corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science studies of large language models, the corpus maps how LLMs shape cognition, behavior, and governance while exposing limitations in embodied knowledge, ethics, and reliability. It documents AI-enabled learning tools, health information dynamics, public-policy experimentation, and sociotechnical deployments, alongside methodological innovations leveraging LLMs and knowledge graphs. A recurring emphasis is on trust, transparency, and equity in AI-based decision-making and education.

themes.name: LLMs as social actors: perception, trust, and ethics
themes.description: Papers examine how users perceive LLMs' humanness and empathy, the risks of anthropomorphism, and ethical implications for trust and social interaction.

themes.name: AI in health and well-being: information dynamics and care
themes.description: A cluster of studies analyzes AI-generated health information, misinformation, patient education, and AI-supported clinical decision-making across diverse populations.

themes.name: AI as a methodological tool for social science
themes.description: A suite of methodological papers proposes LLMS-augmented content analysis, multi-agent simulations, knowledge graphs, and governance frameworks, highlighting validation needs and ethical considerations.

themes.name: AI in education and learning
themes.description: Education-focused work investigates AI tutors, scaffolding models, classroom integration, and implications for assessment, pedagogy, and teacher roles.
